One batch call runs at most 40 journeys inside `budget_seconds` (default 75, max 85, so the answer arrives inside the platform's response time limit). Journeys that could not start are returned in `pending`; resubmit exactly those (benmore verify does this automatically and fails loudly if a batch makes no progress).

A `script` reads and asserts; the steps that change the page belong in `actions`. When the page navigates while the script runs (the redirect after a sign-in click lands), the script is started again on the new page once it has loaded, for up to 3 navigations. A script that itself navigates on every page it runs on fails with `the page navigated 4 times while the script ran`.

Concurrency is a platform setting (default 2, max 8; the result reports it as `concurrency`) shared with browser_check. Each journey runs in its own browser context (separate cookies/storage) inside one Chrome process.

qa_inventory crawls at most 20 pages per call and only follows same-origin page links (API, asset, PDF and sign-out URLs are skipped). It signs in as ONE user per call; run it per role to compare views. Create a dedicated QA user (create_superuser with role:user, or signup) - never crawl as a real customer's account.

Each page carries final_path and redirected_to (alias or login bounce); an anonymous crawl reports login-bounced pages once under auth_gated. Anonymous 401s from the framework's own /api/_auth/* sign-in probe land in expected_auth_probes and do not make a page unclean; signed-in crawls keep the strict oracle.

`benmore verify` always targets the dev instance. Called directly, qa_inventory, browser_batch and browser_check take `env` like every tool: dev by default when the app has a dev instance, prod when it has none or when `env:"prod"` is passed (`benmore qa draft --env prod` does that). Do not run journeys with mutating actions against prod. Sessions minted for `as` live for the call only and are deleted afterwards.
